guideTitle: 5 Best Pull Out Trash Cans in 2026
metaTitle: Best Pull Out Trash Cans, Reviewed (2026)
metaDescription: Five pull out trash can systems for kitchen cabinets compared by size, mounting, soft-close slides and whether bins are included, from Rev-A-Shelf and Insputer.
introParagraphs: A pull out trash can solves the oldest kitchen problem: where to put the bin. Mounted inside a base cabinet, it hides the trash behind a door, frees the floor and slides out on rails when you need it. The catch is that a cabinet is a fixed box, so success depends on measurements far more than on brand or looks.

The five systems below split into two families. Rev-A-Shelf offers the 35-quart Double Pullout with two cans and a metal frame, plus a top mount double that needs a face frame cabinet. Insputer offers a dual 40-quart system with two 10-gallon cans, and two heavy steel frames with soft-close slides that are sold without the cans. Sizes differ by an inch or two, and that inch decides whether the system fits.

We evaluated each system on its listing specs and buyer feedback themes, focusing on required cabinet size, how it mounts, how smoothly it slides and what is included. Read the measurements carefully before ordering, because a pull out that does not fit is a return, not a project.

products.description:
The Insputer dual system is the most capable pull out in this group for a family kitchen. It holds two 40-quart cans, each about 10 gallons, so one side can take trash and the other recycling without a second bin on the floor. The frame is heavy-duty structural steel with a nano-painted surface for high load-bearing capacity.

Soft-close slides make the drawer glide shut quietly and prevent the slam that tips cans on cheaper rails. The listing gives the system's size as 16.1 inches wide, 22.04 deep and 18.9 high, and requires a minimum cabinet of 18 inches wide, 24 deep and 20.6 high. Those figures are the first thing to check, because this system needs a bigger cabinet than the Rev-A-Shelf options.

The larger footprint is the tradeoff: if your cabinet is narrow, it simply will not fit. Compared with the Rev-A-Shelf Double at 35 quarts, it holds more per can but needs a wider opening. Compared with the plain Insputer frames, it includes the cans. For a standard-width base cabinet and a household that recycles, it is the strongest choice.
products.bestFor: Standard base cabinets in homes that sort trash and recycling.
pros: Trash and recycling in one pull out
cons: Needs an 18-inch wide cabinet at minimum

products.description:
The Rev-A-Shelf Double is the compact answer for narrower cabinets. The system measures 14.21 inches wide, 21.65 deep and 19.05 high, and the listing says your cabinet opening must be at least 14.5 wide, 21.75 deep and 19.25 high. That makes it far easier to fit into a typical 15-inch base cabinet than the Insputer dual.

Two 35-quart cans, together with a metal frame, come in the box. A 35-quart bin is about 8.75 gallons according to the maker's own replacement bin listing, so each can is a little smaller than the Insputer's 10 gallons. The system mounts to the cabinet floor with the included hardware, and a separate door-mount kit is needed if you want to attach the cabinet door to the pull out.

The listing advises you to measure cabinet width, depth, height and hinge clearance, which is good advice for every product here. The cans are smaller, and the door kit is an extra. Compared with the Rev-A-Shelf Top Mount, it mounts to the floor rather than the cabinet side. If your cabinet is narrow and you want a proven brand, this is the one to pick.
products.bestFor: Narrower base cabinets that still need trash and recycling.
pros: Fits a cabinet opening of 14.5 inches wide

products.description:
The Top Mount is built for a specific kind of cabinet. It fits only face frame cabinets, with a minimum opening of 15 inches wide, 22.75 deep and 18.35 high, and the listing is firm that you should measure before ordering. If your cabinets are frameless, this system is not for you.

A maple frame goes into the cabinet opening and is secured to the cabinet side with the included mounting hardware, and the listing names it a top mount system for base cabinets that helps keep waste out of sight. Because the frame fastens to the cabinet side, the way it is anchored differs from the floor-mounted Rev-A-Shelf, so read the install notes closely. The system measures 15 inches wide, 22.5 deep and 17.88 high and holds two 35-quart cans.

The fit requirement is stricter than for the floor-mounted Rev-A-Shelf, and installation involves more precise placement. Compared with the Insputer dual, it is smaller but more specialized. Compared with the floor-mount Rev-A-Shelf, it trades a simple install for compatibility with specific cabinets. If your cabinets are face frame and the floor is awkward, this is the right answer.

Heavy-duty structural steel with a nano-painted surface supports the load, and the listing promises detailed instructions so installation should not be difficult. The slides do the work of keeping the bin stable, which is where cheaper systems struggle.

buyingCriteria.explanation: Everything starts with the cabinet. The Rev-A-Shelf Double needs an opening of at least 14.5 inches wide, 21.75 deep and 19.25 high, the Top Mount needs 15 by 22.75 by 18.35, and the Insputer dual needs 18 by 24 by 20.6. Measure width, depth, height and hinge clearance, because a hinge that intrudes into the opening can block the pull out. A system that does not fit cannot be fixed by a screwdriver. Open the cabinet door fully and look for a centre rail, a plumbing pipe, a corner brace or a shelf lip that would reduce the usable opening below the nominal size. Those obstructions are the usual reason a pull out that looked fine on paper refuses to slide.

Floor-mounted systems like the Rev-A-Shelf Double and Insputer sit on the cabinet base, while the Rev-A-Shelf Top Mount is a top mount system whose maple frame is secured to the cabinet side. The Top Mount listing says it fits face frame cabinets only, so frameless cabinets rule it out. Floor mounting, as the Rev-A-Shelf Double describes, attaches to the cabinet floor with included hardware. Check which type your cabinet construction allows before you order, and read the install notes for whichever you choose.

Slides determine how the system feels every day. The Insputer systems list soft-close damping slides that stop the drawer from slamming, which also keeps cans from tipping. Cheap slides rattle and sag when loaded. Pull out heavy cans before trusting them. A full ten-gallon can of bottles and cans is heavy, so the slide rating matters more for a recycling side than for a trash side. Smooth, quiet travel under real load is the best sign that a system will still feel good in a year.

The Rev-A-Shelf cans are 35 quarts, about 8.75 gallons, while the Insputer dual cans are 40 quarts, or 10 gallons. A larger can needs a larger cabinet. Think about whether you need recycling as well as trash. Two 35-quart cans give you roughly 17 gallons in total, while two 40-quart cans give about 20, so the larger Insputer suits a household that cooks daily and sorts waste. A single can in a tiny cabinet is still a gain over a bin on the floor.

Some systems include cans, like the Rev-A-Shelf Double and Insputer dual 40QT, while the other Insputer frames do not. The Rev-A-Shelf door kit is separate. Read the listing so you know what you must buy. A frame without a can is not a working system. Add the cost of cans and any door kit to the headline price before comparing, because a cheap frame plus two bins can end up costing as much as a complete kit. Compare total value, not just the first number you see.

Pull outs require drilling or fastening to the cabinet. Both Insputer and Rev-A-Shelf supply hardware and instructions. A level installation matters, so a helper and a drill make the job easier. If you rent, check whether you may modify cabinets. Mark the screw positions with a pencil and test-fit the frame before drilling, and keep the instruction sheet because slide alignment is easiest to correct before the last screw. Plan an hour or two rather than ten minutes.

howWeEvaluated.title: Fit requirements
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared cabinet minimums from 14.5 inches wide on the Rev-A-Shelf Double to 18 inches on the Insputer dual and noted face frame limits on the Top Mount. Because fit is the single biggest reason pull out systems are returned, we gave it the most weight. A system that suits a wide range of cabinets scored higher than one with narrow requirements.

howWeEvaluated.title: Slides and stability
howWeEvaluated.description: We looked at slide quality as described, especially the soft-close slides on the Insputer systems. The listing for the Rev-A-Shelf systems focuses on fit and mounting rather than slide features, so we did not rank them on slide quality. We treated the soft-close damping as a real convenience that also prevents cans from tipping.

howWeEvaluated.title: What is in the box
howWeEvaluated.description: We separated complete systems with cans from frames sold without them. Complete kits are easier for a first-time buyer, while frames reward people who already know which bins they want. We also noted the separate door-mount kit that the Rev-A-Shelf Double lists.

howWeEvaluated.title: Capacity
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared 35-quart cans on the Rev-A-Shelf with 40-quart cans on the Insputer dual.

howWeEvaluated.title: Why five picks
howWeEvaluated.description: A sixth Rev-A-Shelf listing was a replacement bin rather than a pull out system, so we left it out instead of padding the list.

faq.q: How do I know if a pull out trash can fits my cabinet?
faq.a: Measure the opening width, depth and height, and check hinge clearance. Compare with the listed minimums, such as 14.5 by 21.75 by 19.25 inches for the Rev-A-Shelf Double. If you are within a hair, choose a smaller system. A tight fit can bind the slides or rub the cabinet walls, and then the whole point of a smooth pull out is lost. When in doubt, ask the maker for the exact clearances before you order.

faq.q: What is the difference between top mount and floor mount?
faq.a: A floor mount sits on the cabinet base, while a top mount hangs from the cabinet side or top. The Rev-A-Shelf Top Mount fits face frame cabinets only. Pick the style that matches your cabinets. If you are not sure whether yours has a face frame, look at the front of the cabinet box: a raised wooden frame around the opening means face frame, and a flush front means frameless. That one check saves a return.

faq.q: Do pull out systems come with trash cans?
faq.a: Some do and some do not. The Rev-A-Shelf Double and Insputer 40QT include cans, while two Insputer frames do not. Check the listing before ordering. Frames without cans can still be a good buy if you already own bins that fit. Buy the cans and the frame together if you want to be certain they match.
Yes. They prevent slamming and keep cans from tipping, as the Insputer listings point out. Cheap slides can sag and rattle.

faq.q: Can I install a pull out myself?
faq.a: Most people with basic tools can. Both brands supply hardware and instructions. A helper makes leveling easier.

faq.q: Can I attach the cabinet door?
faq.a: Some systems allow it. The Rev-A-Shelf Double needs a separate door-mount kit. Without it, the door opens independently.

faq.q: How much weight can a pull out hold?
faq.a: Check the listing. The Insputer frames are heavy-duty steel meant for high load-bearing capacity. Avoid overloading the cans. Heavy glass and wet kitchen waste weigh more than they look, so empty the cans before they are completely full to protect both the slides and the bags.
